prize_parts.citation: for credible empirical analysis of how import competition and technological change reshape labour demand, wages and local labour-market adjustment

statement.case_for: My configuration has changed since round 1. I now prefer B037 with Autor, Dorn and Hanson, and I move B022 to an alternative. My round-1 reservations about B037 were that two strands were bundled, that the long-run interpretation of the China shock is contested, and that credit for the technology strand is diffuse. The exchange addressed most of these. Several members (Hassler, Dreber, Fredriksson) now accept that the Autor-Dorn-Hanson import-shock papers are a coherent, jointly authored body of work. They also accept that the citation should rest on credibly identified evidence about adjustment, not on a settled verdict on effect sizes. On the chair's question, I read the discovery as one achievement: exposure to trade and technology shocks reallocates labour demand, and the adjustment costs are concentrated, slow and persistent at the local level. The evidence is transparent, design-based and replicated in other countries, and the debates over magnitude are the kind that follow a mature programme. The trio keeps the technology and task evidence through Autor without naming Katz, so the citation does not claim the whole skill-premium literature. It also avoids the closest overlap with the 2023 prize. I weigh this on identification credibility, breadth of lesson and clarity of attribution. Support counts are not part of the case. On my own B022, I accepted in round 1 that this is a method rather than a discovery about economic phenomena, and the exchange did not weaken that objection. I would keep B022 as the most serious alternative to B037 on durability and cross-field use, but not as the lead.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation remains that B037 may be two discoveries. A trio built around the import-shock evidence under-credits the long-run skill-premium framework and Katz. If the committee thinks that framework is the main achievement, this configuration is wrong. The task framework also owes much to Levy, Murnane and Acemoglu, who is already a laureate, so the citation cannot claim it. The size and persistence of the China-shock effects and the robustness of shift-share designs are still debated, and the core papers (about 2013) are younger than B022, B001 or B045. The topic also sits near the 2023 and 2024 prizes on labour markets, skills and technology. I moved from a first-place ranking for B022 to B037 in part because my objections to B037 were addressed. I should check whether I am being drawn along by the number of colleagues who prefer it. I do not count that as scientific merit.

responses.point: Hassler (chair) moved from Katz to Autor, Dorn and Hanson. He ties the citation to empirical analysis of adjustment, says Autor carries the task and polarisation strand, and prefers Dorn to Katz because of overlap with the 2023 and 2024 prizes. He concedes that this leaves out the long-run education-versus-technology framing.
responses.response: I now hold the same trio, and I changed my own view rather than adopting his. His framing of the cost is the right one: the committee should accept openly that this choice leaves out the long-run education-versus-technology framing. Crediting the task strand through Autor is defensible, but I would not let the citation imply the trio originated the task model. I note that he and I co-authored a paper (IJIO 2026) and that he is the chair, so our agreement should not be counted as independent evidence. My reasons are the attribution structure of the import-shock papers and the changed wording of the citation.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson prefers Autor, Hanson and Katz. She calls the Dorn variant (my opening trio) a defensible alternative that covers the trade-shock strand more tightly, and says the committee should decide Katz versus Dorn on attribution grounds, not by default. She regards the overlap of Katz's work with Goldin's prize as partial.
responses.response: I take that to be the right way to frame the choice, and my answer on attribution is Dorn. He is a full co-author of the central papers, and omitting him would misstate where the evidence came from. I accept her view that the Goldin overlap is partial, so I do not rest my choice on it. What decides it for me is that Katz's strand has the more diffuse credit structure and the more contested boundary with prior recognition. A Katz trio is a coherent alternative and I would not oppose it on scientific grounds. If the committee judges the skill-premium framework to be the core discovery, then Katz belongs in the prize and my configuration under-credits it. I cannot settle that here.

responses.point: Enflo prefers Autor, Hanson and Katz. She argues that my trio narrows the prize to the trade strand and drops the skill-premium and task framework that gives the trade evidence its general meaning. She says Dorn in place of Katz is defensible and she has not resolved it.
responses.response: The narrowing is real, and it is the price of cleaner attribution. I answer it by having the citation say 'import competition and technological change', so the general lesson about labour demand is kept without naming the whole framework. I agree with her that the trade-shock designs are the part with the strongest replication. I disagree that the framework is needed to make them interpretable. The local-labour-market evidence stands on its own identification. Her stated fallback of moving to Autor, Dorn and Hanson if the committee prefers a narrower prize shows that our positions are close. The disagreement is over scope, and I do not think it is a dispute about merit.

responses.point: Andersson ranks B022 first with Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes. He agrees on the BLP core, keeps Levinsohn over Bresnahan, and notes that his and my agreement on B022 should be treated with caution because of our overlapping interest in applied microeconomics.
responses.response: I share that caution about our agreement, and it is one reason I am stepping back from B022 as my lead. On the chair's question about what would put B022 above B037, I would need the committee to judge the three B037 attribution problems unresolvable (two discoveries, an unsettled third name, and overlap with recent prizes) and to treat structural estimation as a discovery rather than a method. What would keep it below B037 is that B022 is mainly a methodological contribution and that the Bresnahan and Reiss exclusions are a real cost. I still regard B022 as a mature, durable prize with the BLP core clear. I keep it as my first alternative, and a BLP prize would not be a mistake.

uncertainties: Whether the committee treats the technology and task strand and the import-shock strand as one discovery. If it does not, my trio honours only one part and under-credits Katz's skill-premium work.
How large and persistent the China-shock effects are, and how robust shift-share identification is. I have not checked the underlying papers independently.
Whether adjacency to the 2023 and 2024 prizes should lower the weight of B037, and whether Dorn is a better third name than Katz on grounds other than that overlap.

Whether my move away from B022 reflects a real change in my assessment or some drift toward the prevailing position. I tried to base it on the changed wording and attribution rather than on support counts.

How a method that changed practice (B022) should be weighed against a replicated empirical programme (B037) and a framework with open puzzles (B001). I rely on my own knowledge of the literature and the colleagues' round-1 files, and have not verified sources independently.
statement.conflict_note: No connection to Autor, Dorn or Hanson is apparent from my supplied profile. My co-authors named there are not on B037. I work in industrial organisation, adjacent to B022, which is now an alternative. I co-authored with Committee chair John Hassler and former chair Tore Ellingsen (IJIO 2026). Hassler now supports the same trio, and I do not treat our agreement as independent evidence. I am also an SSE colleague of Dreber Almenberg, Strömberg and Andersson, which is a tie between members and not to any candidate. My spouse is a former Swedish prime minister. This is a public fact and I see no bearing on any shortlisted candidate. All of this is disclosed and not adjudicated.
